nodes.title: Algebra
nodes.description: Tests fluency with linear equations, inequalities, functions, and systems, including their graphs and real-world interpretations. Alongside Advanced Math it makes up the largest share of the Math section, appearing as both multiple-choice and grid-in items across all modules.

nodes.title: Linear Equations in One Variable
nodes.description: Solve and create linear equations in one variable, including equations with fractional or decimal coefficients, and interpret their solutions and graphs. Items often embed the equation in a real-world word problem.

nodes.title: Linear Functions
nodes.description: Evaluate, define, and interpret linear functions: read slope and intercept in context, build an f(x) = mx + b model from a scenario or table, and compare two linear functions to answer a question.

nodes.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
nodes.description: Solve and create linear equations in two variables, interpret their graphs — slope, x- and y-intercepts — and connect an equation to the line and to the real-world quantities it describes.

nodes.title: Systems of Linear Equations
nodes.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables and interpret the number of solutions (one, none, or infinitely many) in terms of the graphs and the real-world situation they model.

nodes.title: Linear Inequalities
nodes.description: Solve and graph linear inequalities in one or two variables, interpret inequality notation and constraint regions, and solve systems of inequalities to find feasible solutions.

nodes.title: Advanced Math
nodes.description: Tests nonlinear mathematics — quadratic and higher-degree functions, equivalent expressions, and systems of nonlinear equations — and the ability to build, manipulate, and interpret them. Alongside Algebra it makes up the largest share of the Math section.

nodes.title: Equivalent Expressions
nodes.description: Recognize and produce equivalent forms of algebraic expressions — through expansion, factoring, and rewriting — and use the structure of these forms to reason about coefficients, values, and solutions.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Functions
nodes.description: Evaluate, interpret, and graph nonlinear functions such as quadratics and other polynomials, including maximums, minimums, roots, and end behavior, and build or transform these functions from given conditions.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Equations and Systems
nodes.description: Solve equations and systems involving nonlinear (e.g., quadratic or rational) equations — by factoring, the quadratic formula, or graphing — and interpret the solutions and their real-world context.

nodes.title: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis
nodes.description: Tests quantitative reasoning about ratios, percentages, proportional relationships, and data shown in tables, graphs, and statistics. Questions emphasize interpreting quantities and evaluating claims in real-world contexts rather than mechanical computation.

nodes.title: Ratios, Rates, and Proportional Relationships
nodes.description: Set up and solve problems involving ratios, unit rates, and direct proportions, including converting units and scaling quantities, and interpret proportional relationships in real-world context.

nodes.title: Percentages
nodes.description: Solve percentage problems including percent increase and decrease, percent of a quantity, repeated or compound percent changes, and reverse-percent (back-solving) applications.

nodes.title: One-Variable Data
nodes.description: Represent and analyze distributions of a single variable — measures of center (mean, median, mode) and spread (range, standard deviation) — and interpret how changes to the data values affect them.

nodes.title: Two-Variable Data
nodes.description: Analyze relationships between two variables in tables and scatterplots, including association and correlation, and model trends with lines of best fit, interpreting the meaning of the fit's slope and intercept.

nodes.title: Probability and Conditional Probability
nodes.description: Compute and interpret probabilities and conditional probabilities from two-way tables and other representations, expressing the likelihood of events and outcomes in a clear numeric or percent form.

nodes.title: Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
nodes.description: Reason about samples and margin of error: use a random sample's statistic to estimate a population characteristic, interpret the margin of error in terms of precision, and connect sample size to reliability.

nodes.title: Evaluating Claims
nodes.description: Assess whether a conclusion about a population is justified by the data — distinguishing correlation from causation, evaluating experimental versus observational designs, and checking whether a conclusion follows from the given survey or study.

nodes.title: Geometry and Trigonometry
nodes.description: Tests measurement and spatial reasoning: area, volume, lines and angles, triangle relationships, right-triangle trigonometry, and circle properties. A smaller but consistent share of the Math section, delivered partly as figure-based multiple-choice items.

nodes.title: Area and Volume
nodes.description: Compute areas and volumes of geometric figures, including composite shapes, apply scaling principles when dimensions change, and connect these measures to real-world objects and contexts.

nodes.title: Lines, Angles, and Triangles
nodes.description: Use properties of lines, angles, parallel lines and transversals, and triangle relationships — including congruence and similarity — to find missing angle measures and side relationships.

nodes.title: Right Triangles and Trigonometry
nodes.description: Apply the Pythagorean theorem and right-triangle trigonometry (sine, cosine, tangent) to solve for missing sides and angles, including in applied contexts and coordinate-plane problems.

nodes.title: Circles
nodes.description: Solve for measures related to circles — radius, diameter, circumference, area, arcs, sectors, and central and inscribed angle relationships — and interpret equations of circles in the coordinate plane.
